data.why: The repo's bundled data/sample/*.txt (13 input/static files for all 19 districts) is a complete, self-consistent example dataset already matched to src/district/config.py's expected schema; the Streamlit entry point itself (app.py) was removed from this repo during an upstream migration to a FastAPI-only service (see MIGRATED.md, api.py), so it was reconstructed as a seed file around the untouched src/district/scheduler.py core to restore the documented UI.

goals: Run the baseline daily supply-demand schedule for all 19 river districts using the bundled sample inflow/demand/reservoir data and read off total demand, supply and shortage
Identify which districts show a water shortage ('缺水(浙东需供)') under the sample scenario and by how much
Inspect a single district's day-by-day storage trajectory (日初/日中/日末容积, 排水, 蓄水) to see how its reservoir is operated over the simulation window
Compare the inflow vs. demand time series for a chosen district to judge how close it runs to its target water level
Upload a modified ZIP of input/static files (e.g. a scaled-down inflow scenario) and compare resulting total shortage against the baseline run
Export a chosen district's full daily balance table to Excel for offline analysis

review.summary: The tree describes this reconstructed 19-district daily water-balance tool well. The run → review by district → export phases are right, the labels are faithful, and most checked screens match its numbers, including the per-district shortage sums and storage readings. It needs fixes before filing: the chart-export evidence is wrong, the uploaded-scenario comparison (a core README use) has no node, t2 is padding, and f1/f3/f5 carry a few claims nobody confirmed.
